claims.locator: Introduction, quote 'The conclusions of the additional research are'
claims.sourceText: The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997), Introduction, 'The conclusions of the additional research are'
claims.text: The report's conclusions are that Air Force activities spanning many years were consolidated into two or three days of July 1947; that the 'aliens' were probably anthropomorphic test dummies carried aloft by high altitude balloons; that the 'unusual' military activity was balloon launch and recovery; and that the hospital-bodies claims most likely combine a 1956 KC-97 crash in which eleven airmen died with a 1959 manned balloon mishap injuring two pilots.

claims.text: The certified morning reports of the 427th AAF Base Unit Squadron 'M' show five Army Nurse Corps nurses at Roswell AAF in July 1947; none reassigned on 8 or 9 July 1947; one reassigned 23 July 1947 to Fort Worth AAF by normal rotation and on active duty there until March 1949; none transferred overseas or killed in a plane crash.

edges.note: The GAO inquiry that produced the Air Force reports was initiated by Rep. Reasoning: the report's structure tracks the books' witness list.

edges.note: Section 1.4 argues that Maltais and Knight may have confused the Plains with San Agustin Pass or Peak, adjacent to White Sands and the Jornada Test Range, where numerous dummy flights terminated.

b.label: The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert (1995)

edges.label: The 1997 report completes what the 1994-1995 report left open
edges.note: The 1994 report addressed the debris and did not address the bodies claims; the 1997 report was produced to close that gap.

edges.label: Two official inquiries that explained the recovery activity without producing the logs
edges.note: The Brazilian Army's 2010 inquiry explained the Varginha vehicle movements as routine maintenance and school transport; the USAF's 1997 report explained the New Mexico recovery teams as dummy-recovery operations. Both are plausible and neither published the underlying unit movement records. Reasoning: an explanation of activity is not the same artifact as the activity log.

edges.label: The 1997 report dismantled the 'missing nurse' account by name
edges.note: Section 2.1 uses 427th AAFBU Squadron 'M' morning reports and National Personnel Records Center searches to show 'Naomi Maria Selff' never served, and identifies 1st Lt. Eileen M. Fanton as matching every other particular.
